messages.subject: [R-SIG-Finance] Tidy finance use
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I'm trying to use the tidyfinance, tidyverse, tidyquant packages to no
avail. My setup is R version 4.5.1 in OSX 11.7.1. I'm trying to compile
examples from the book Tidy Finance with R, Scheuch, C, Voigt, S, Weiss,
P.  The error I'm receiving is below.

prices <- tq_get("AAPL",
  get = "stock.prices",
  from = "2021-01-01", to = "2026-12-31")

prices |>
ggplot(aes(x = date, y = adjusted)) + geom_line() +
labs(
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL,
    title = "Apple stock prices between beginning of 2000 and end of 2021"
)

The lines above work fine however the code below does not. Any suggestions,
please.

returns <- prices |>
arrange(date) |>
mutate(ret = adjusted / lag(adjusted) - 1) |> select(symbol, date, ret)
returns

Error in select(mutate(arrange(prices, date), ret = adjusted/lag(adjusted)
-  :
  unused arguments (symbol, date, ret)

R> standardGeneric for "returns" defined from package "timeSeries"

function (x, ...)
standardGeneric("returns")
<bytecode: 0x7fddbb02feb0>
<environment: 0x7fddbb019890>
Methods may be defined for arguments: x
Use  showMethods(returns)  for currently available ones.

Could this be due to the timeSeries package, some sort of compatibility
issue?

TIA,

--
Andr? Luiz Tietbohl Ramos, PhD.

messages.subject: [R-SIG-Finance] Tidy finance use
messages.body_plain:
If I had to guess, it's probably the lag function, as the default in
tidyverse has a one-period look-AHEAD, whereas stats::lag (the correct
function) has it one period *behind*.

For the error line, in R/Finance lingo, you'd do

returns <- Return.calculate(Ad(<<your symbol here>>))

But in any case, it's generally good practice NOT to use the tidyverse in
general, in my opinion. The data.table library is superior for general data
analysis, and it's absolutely no-go once you get to finance, since it
overrides first, last, lag, and filter functions in ways that can easily
make code break.

The only time I'd use tidyverse functionality is with ggplot2. Other than
that, the usual xts, quantmod, and PerformanceAnalytics packages should
have all the functionality you need.

Is there a particular reason you want to use tidyverse packages?
